messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Observability gap detected for tenant=OrionHealth (dedicated pool us-west-2). Missing traces / spans; metrics partially present. Paging on-call SREs @sara and runtime @mike.

sara: on it. quick summary? what's the customer impact?

mike: spans for OrionHealth are not showing up in the traces UI or in the APM backend. Logs still arrive for most services, but trace/span IDs are absent. Their request-level metrics look normal for most routes, but latency histograms for a few routes are empty (weird).

ashwin: confirmed. the forwarder instances in us-west-2 are applying a tenant-filter step during env parsing. recent deploy (2026-03-12 03:14 UTC) changed the allowed-tenant list and OrionHealth's tenant header got excluded by mistake. we didn't add a migration for older s3-sharded buffers so some spans are being dropped at ingest.

jen: can we flip the fallback path? there's a fallback forwarder pool that bypasses the new filter. i can enable it.

sara: yes please. enable fallback, but also prepare to rollback the filter config if that doesn't stitch spans back for >10m. jen, paste the exact command you plan to run.

jen: running the toggle now — calling internal API: 
```
# enable per-tenant-fallback in us-west-2 forwarder group
curl -X POST https://internal-config.redwood/api/v1/forwarder/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONFIG_OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"region":"us-west-2","feature":"tenant-fallback","state":"on"}'
```

mike: starting rollout: kubectl -n forwarders set image deployment/forwarder-usw2 forwarder=image@sha:abcdef1 && kubectl rollout restart deployment/forwarder-usw2. will watch logs for reingest hints.

ashwin: note — older s3 shard prefix for OrionHealth is at s3://redwood-buffer/us-west-2/shards/orionhealth/2026-03-11. we can run a span-replay job to reingest missing spans once reads are allowed. need a temporary IAM role for the job to read that bucket.

mike: creating the replay job now. sample command: 
```
# kick off span replay for OrionHealth (dry-run then real)
kubectl run span-replay-orion --image=redwood/replay:prod --restart=OnFailure -- \
  --replay-bucket=s3://redwood-buffer/us-west-2/shards/orionhealth --tenant=orionhealth --mode=apply
```

ashwin: i'll provision short-term cross-account read and attach to the replay job service account. creating IAM policy and role: 
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject","s3:ListBucket"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-buffer/us-west-2/shards/orionhealth/*"]
    }
  ]
}
```

sam-account: account team — heads up, OrionHealth support already flagged gaps in their dashboards. please hold customer comms until we have an ETA for reingest; they'll want a timeline for missing spans (likely covering ~03:10–03:30 UTC).

sara: ack. mike/jen — how long to verify fallback works and to run a small replay?

mike: fallback toggled, forwarder pods rolling; i see a burst of span telemetry coming in but mapping is partial. looks like some spans lacked tenant headers on earlier requests, so they may be lost. replay queued, estimated runtime ~18m for the 30GB shard.

jen: after toggle, traces reappeared for a subset of requests — p50/p90 now populated for some endpoints. still missing for two routes that use an internal proxy that strips headers.

ashwin: that explains it — proxy config (envoy) had a recent change that removed `x-tenant-id` on certain upstream calls. two options: 1) patch proxy to preserve header and replay, or 2) backfill using request logs correlated by request_id. patching proxy is safer but will require restart of a small fleet.

mike: i'm going to patch envoy to add `x-tenant-id` to upstream for those routes and restart. rolling restart now (min-availability 80%).

incident-bot: state update — rollback not required at this time. tenant-fallback enabled. span-replay job started (ID: replay-2134567890-1). paging window extended to 60m.

jen: span-replay logs show successful read from s3 and ~92% of spans requeued for ingestion. a minority failed due to missing request_id mapping. still, we should see significant improvement once replay completes.

sam-account: updating OrionHealth: suggested msg — short note acknowledging impact, we are ingesting historical spans and expect >90% restoration within 30m, we'll follow up with details and postmortem. want me to send?

sara: please send now. keep it transparent, call out ETA and mitigation. cc: account team + eng contact.

sam-account: sending now. (sends customer message) :email:

mike: replay job finished. most traces are back in the UI; p95/p99 histograms look consistent with pre-incident. two endpoints still partial — correlated to missing request_id in logs.

ashwin: created a short-term alert in CI so future config changes that touch tenant filters must run per-tenant acceptance tests against a dummy tenant header. also filed a runbook task: RB-512 to add strong validation to forwarder deploys.

jen: rolling back the forwarder config PR that removed the tenant entry and adding the acceptance test now.

incident-bot: incident bridged to postmortem workflow. severity: P1 -> mitigated. follow-up owners: eng-runtime (mike), eng-sre (sara), infra-config (ashwin).

sara: great work everyone. main action items — 1) finish forwarder PR & acceptance test, 2) add proxy header-preserve e2e, 3) verify S3 replay coverage and automate. i'll open the postmortem doc and assign.

mike: will attach logs and replay artifacts to the postmortem.

jen: leaving a note: consider adding a telemetry sanity check at ingest gates to detect tenant-less spans and surface them to deploy previews.

sam-account: customer confirmed they can see restored traces and appreciate the quick updates. closing comms after we finalize the postmortem.

sara: closing thread here, moving to postmortem doc. thanks all :heart:
